html:
An unwritten agreement made in 1943 by the leaders of Lebanon's religious communities, which set how they would share power in the new independent state.

Its makers were the Maronite Christian president Bechara El Khoury and the Sunni Muslim prime minister Riad Al Solh. Lebanon was then under the French mandate and won its independence later that year. The pact settled two fears. The Christians would not seek French protection, and the Muslims would not seek to join Lebanon to Syria; Lebanon would be an independent country with an Arab face.

Top posts were fixed by sect:

  • the president a Maronite Christian;
  • the prime minister a Sunni Muslim;
  • the speaker of parliament a Shia Muslim;
  • seats in parliament split six Christians to five Muslims, based on the census of 1932.

The system kept the peace for three decades but froze the balance of 1943 as populations changed. Muslim anger at Christian dominance was one cause of the civil war of 1975. The Taif Agreement of 1989 changed the shares to half and half, but kept posts tied to sect.
sum: An unwritten agreement made in 1943 by the leaders of Lebanon's religious communities, which set how they would share power in the new independent state.
